sources.readScope: HTTP transport scope, protected-resource discovery, resource parameter and token handling sections
sources.observation: HTTP MCP authorization uses protected-resource metadata and resource-bound tokens. Audience validation belongs to the resource server; invalid/expired tokens receive401, and tokens must not go in query strings. This is a selected dated protocol revision, not a live provider compatibility result.

sources.readScope: Description, stream specifiers, bounded allocation and selected format/stream/packet/frame output options
sources.observation: ffprobe distinguishes containers and streams and exposes JSON, packet/frame data and per-stream selectors. A URL input initiates network access; max_alloc limits a single allocation rather than total process memory. No ffprobe runtime was executed.

sources.readScope: Model variants, inference dependencies, limitations and non-commercial section
sources.observation: FaceID uses InsightFace embedding with LoRA; Plus adds CLIP structure and Portrait uses multiple views. The model card explicitly restricts the models to research/non-commercial use and admits imperfect identity consistency. This prevents commercial default admission regardless of the root adapter code license.

sources.readScope: Selected introduction, dataset tradeoffs, evaluation and implementation sections; not full appendix
sources.observation: CameraCtrl conditions on Plucker embeddings and evaluates camera rotation/translation separately using reconstructed trajectories. RealEstate10K was chosen for appearance/trajectory diversity. Published metrics are the authors results, not local measurements; reconstruction uncertainty remains important for generated/deforming scenes.

sources.readScope: Selected interactive refinement and memory-bank architecture descriptions; no full-paper review claimed
sources.observation: SAM2 maintains recent/prompted-frame memories and lightweight object pointers for cross-frame segmentation. Prompt correction and memory propagation enable interactive tracking, but object segmentation alone does not prove fine alpha matting or temporal repair quality.

Feedback TOP uses a downstream Target TOP, bypass/reset input behavior and one-frame reset pulse. Resolution, pixel format and Info CHOP cook/memory/error channels are explicit. Native runtime execution has not occurred.

sources.readScope: Description, Analyze capture, timing/log overhead and CPU/GPU distinction
sources.observation: Analyze captures frame events with less disturbance than continuous output. Most TOP cook times measure issuing GPU work rather than actual GPU processing; therefore low CPU cook duration does not certify frame latency.

sources.readScope: Selected summary, alpha selection, audio CHOP, fps and length settings
sources.observation: Movie File Out supports movie/still/sequence outputs; alpha requires a compatible codec/pixel format. Audio input must be time-sliced, and movie fps/record length are explicit settings. Export parity must be measured in actual decoded output.

sources.readScope: Modal exclusivity, awaited target, cancellation, progress and history-state sections
sources.observation: Photoshop mutations need executeAsModal with awaited completion. Cancellation must interrupt work and exceptions must not be swallowed. History suspension groups edits; it does not authorize unrelated document changes.

sources.readScope: Selected closepath semantics and path grammar
sources.observation: Z closes a subpath and resets current point to its start. Closing with a coincident lineto has different stroke cap/join semantics. Export validation must preserve these distinctions.

sources.readScope: Selected cancellation and promise-state behavior; not entire specification
sources.observation: Canceling removes animation effects by resolving current time to an unresolved state and rejects relevant ready/finished promises. Implementations must account for cancellation and preserve usable content/focus.

sources.readScope: Performance reference, virtual/live alignment, lighting, preview parity and eyeline/techvis sections
sources.observation: The production account emphasizes performance reference, camera/lens registration, timed lighting match, depth compositing, preview/final reflectance consistency and precise eyelines. These become separate MGR acceptance dimensions; the account supplies neither proprietary code nor a reusable Hollywood quality certificate.

sources.readScope: Studio production overview and declared technical work
sources.observation: Weta identifies water/facial animation, underwater performance capture, realtime depth compositing and performance-driven eyelines as major areas. This is studio-reported scope, not implementation source or a matched output benchmark.

sources.readScope: Selected config/linear working-space and compositing overview; page warns its overview is OCIOv1 material
sources.observation: OCIO executes transforms defined by its configuration. A file extension does not identify color encoding; color and non-color data need distinct interpretation. The page warns the overview is legacyv1 and is used for concepts, not current API contracts.
